title: Singing Sonny Boy for the Germans; Hans Buerman
summary: He sang Sonny Boy and German songs for the officers' club, and a soldier who had heard him play at Knokke as a teenager, Hans Buerman, offered papers.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And he says, can you sing and I says yes, I think so and I know the songs that he, that German club -- so, first they love "Sonny Boy."
I grabbed "Sonny Boy" and turned him on. And I wasn't kidding. I wasn't jiving. I was not jiving, man.
And then, there was a song called "Dein ist mein gotzt Herzt
And it was popular at that time. I sang that and then that song "Wien, Wien, nur du Allien."
So, now, the next day, where I was living, I heard boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, at the door.

And a little girl that I had met, she was -- she was saying, oh, don't don't kill him, don't kill him, and she, and he said, nobody's going to kill him. And when I looked -- and so, he says, I'm (inaudible)., and I says, don't I know you?
He said yes, Butler, I know you from Knokke.. You played in Knokke.. He was -- around fourteen, fifteen years old and he liked the trumpet and he was on a vacation there in Knokke..

So, he says now, don't worry about nothing. Come to my office tomorrow and I have what you need. I've got all this -- give you a card, you must have a card of identity and I'll give you a ration card and whatever you need.
